newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM warns Peru hostage crisis could worsen.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM warns Peru hostage crisis could worsen.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Thursday welcomed the release of seven hostages from the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, but said the crisis was likely to intensify.
"The situation is becoming more tense as the number of hostages nears a level the guerrillas can control," Hashimoto told reporters after visiting the Foreign Ministry crisis operation room.
In an apparent gesture of conciliation on New Year's Day, the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) freed seven hostages, including four Japanese businessmen.

But the rebels, who showed no sign of giving in to demands they end the 15-day-old standoff, still hold 74 others captive in the diplomatic compound, including Japanese Ambassador to Peru Morihisa Aoki.
Hashimoto, who cancelled New Year's holiday plans to stay in Tokyo to monitor the crisis, criticised members of the Japanese and other media who made unauthorised contact with the rebels.

Tuesday's incident, in which reporters entered the compound and held interviews with the rebels, made it difficult for the Peruvian government to proceed with negotiations with the rebels by giving the guerrillas a chance to present their views to the world, Hashimoto said.
